blocks.text:
**Dates:** 30 December 2026 – 8 January 2027  

The journey then takes on a very different mood. From Rio, you fly to Iguazu to see the falls from both sides of the border. The Brazilian side offers a broad panorama of the cascades, while the Argentine side leads along walkways above and below the rushing water to Devil’s Throat. The final 3 nights are devoted to a beach holiday. The standard programme takes you to Búzios, but you can choose Angra dos Reis or one of the resorts in north-eastern Brazil.

## What to expect on this journey

### New Year’s Eve on Copacabana

By the evening of 31 December, the beach becomes Rio’s main celebration venue. Thousands of people arrive dressed in white. Flowers, candles and offerings to Iemanjá are left by the water. Performers take to the stages, and as midnight approaches, everyone along the shore turns towards the ocean.

Fireworks are launched from platforms at sea. Bursts of light rise above the dark water, reflect on the waves and stretch along the beach. The music and celebrations continue after midnight.

### Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer

The ascent of Corcovado is by train through tropical forest. From the viewing platform beside the Christ statue, you can see Guanabara Bay, the beaches, hills and neighbourhoods of the city. It is a particularly good place to appreciate how Rio lies between the mountains and the ocean.

### Sugar Loaf

The cable car starts at Red Beach. Its first stop is Urca Hill, followed by a second ascent to the 396-metre summit of Sugar Loaf. From the top, you can see Copacabana, Ipanema, Guanabara Bay, the Niterói Bridge and Corcovado.

### Iguazu Falls

Iguazu is a system of more than 270 cascades stretching for almost 3 kilometres along the border between Brazil and Argentina. In January, during the rainy season, the falls are especially full.

On the Brazilian side, you see a panoramic view of the falls and Devil’s Throat. The Argentine side offers the lower and upper circuits and an approach to the main cascade along an extensive network of walkways.

### Búzios and the tropical coast

After festive Rio and two busy days at the falls, the final days are spent by the ocean. Búzios has sheltered bays with almost calm water as well as open beaches with wind and waves. You can swim, snorkel, windsurf and water-ski, hire a buggy or go sailing.
